Apple recently replaced a billboard in Milan that originally depicted a young child holding an iPhone, as part of its latest "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign. Here are the details.

Apple Removes Controversial Italian Billboard

A few days ago, Italy's child rights watchdog, the Autorità Garante per l'Infanzia e l'Adolescenza (AGIA), publicly condemned Apple for depicting a young child holding an iPhone in its "Relax, it's iPhone" advertising campaign.

The campaign focuses on highlighting the durability and ruggedness of the iPhone, showcasing various scenarios in which the device could be damaged—including someone taking photos in heavy rain, someone placing an iPhone on the edge of a bathtub while watching videos, a dog biting an iPhone, and a young child clumsily holding the device.

After the billboard depicting the final scenario was erected on via Melchiorre Gioia in Milan, AGIA immediately received a public complaint letter stating that the advertisement normalises the behaviour of a "digital babysitter".

AGIA expressed agreement and referred the case to Italy's communications regulator AGCOM, the Italian competition authority AGCM, and the local advertising industry's self-regulatory body IAP, "for appropriate review and any possible action".

According to reports by Prima Comunicazione and Repubblica Milano, Apple has removed the controversial billboard and replaced it with one promoting the "Find My" feature.

Apple has yet to respond publicly to the incident, but its swift action reflects that the company is indeed taking these criticisms seriously—even though the original intent of the advertisement was to showcase the iPhone's durability, the outside interpretation was entirely different.

What are your thoughts on this controversy? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
